content.title: 8 Most Flattering Short Hairstyles for Women Over 50, as Worn by Celebrities
content.text: Skip to main contentThe 8 Short Hairstyles Women Over 50 Want Right NowChristopher Polk/2026GG/Getty ImagesAll products featured on Vogue are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links.When it comes to age, there’s no such thing as hairstyle rules (Embrace the gray. Go super-long. You do you.). But short hairstyles are a go-to for many as they get older for a reason: Our hair changes drastically over time, and the goal is no longer just about personal preference, but about functionality as well.“[Hair] gets finer, loses density, and dries out because the scalp produces less oil. Gray and white hair is coarser and more porous, which changes how it takes color and responds to products. Curl patterns can shift, too,” says celebrity hairstylist David von Cannon. “All of this is why the cut that worked for years might evolve as one gets older.”“The goal becomes less about fighting these changes and more about working with them strategically,” adds Joseph Maine, global artistic director of ColorWow and cofounder of Trademark Beauty.So, other than being chic and effortless, short hairstyles come with loads of benefits. It creates the illusion of fullness and lift, says Maine, and can help give you some softness and shape.If you’re looking for some inspo, below are the eight short hairstyles for women over 50 that are asking for right now (and how to style them), straight from the pros.ExpandJB LacroixThe Blunt BobThe bob continues its reign as the most in-demand cut of the year, especially with women over 50. “I hear it constantly,” says Von Cannon. The most requested type, he says, is the blunt bob, which has that clean, sharp line at the edges to give you a modern feel.To style, he likes to start with a heat protectant like L’Oreal’s EverPure Iron Sleek Coat before blowing hair out. Use a round brush to smooth and do a single pass with a flat iron to keep hair looking sleek (or to add a little flick at the ends for a nice added touch).ExpandMonica Schipper/Getty ImagesThe BixieHalf bob and half pixie, Maine says the bixie is another super-popular option for women over 50 looking to change up their look. To style, you’ll want to apply a lightweight styling cream or paste (we happen to like ROZ’s Evergreen Style Cream) and use your fingers instead of a brush to set hair in place and give it a more lived-in look. Add a texture spray to create more separation and volume.ExpandStefanie Keenan/Getty ImagesThe Textured BobFor women with naturally curly and coily hair, Von Cannon loves a textured bob. He says to opt with a cut that provides more movement so that you don’t have a heavy shape weighing the entire look down.He says to skip the heat and opt for air drying or diffusing. Look for mousse like the Crown Affair Texturizing Air Dry Mousse or the Pattern Curl Mousse to add movement and a soft hold without any crunch.ExpandJEAN BAPTISTE LACROIX/Getty ImagesThe Layered ShagThere’s just something so effortlessly cool about a shag. Maine recommends opting for face-framing layers and to either air dry with a curl cream or diffuse with something like the Kenra Volume Mousse to give hair an extra lift.ExpandDia Dipasupil/Getty ImagesThe Graduated BobAdding another bob into the mix, Von Cannon says that a graduated bob never really goes out of style. “It’s a classic [women] keep coming back to,” he says.For a graduated bob, he recommends a blowout with volume at the crown. To lock it all in, he recommends using a medium hold spray.Audrey Noble is a contributing writer at Vogue, covering all things beauty and wellness.
